requirements.original: **omit: the optional field, in which it is used, is not present;**
requirements.canonical: The `omit` matching mechanism matches if the optional field in which it is used is not present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **omit: the optional field, in which it is used, is not present;**

requirements.original: NOTE 1: **omit can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.** **omit can only be used for matching optional fields.**
requirements.canonical: `omit` CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- NOTE 1: **omit can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.** **omit can only be used for matching optional fields.**

requirements.original: NOTE 1: **omit can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.** **omit can only be used for matching optional fields.**
requirements.canonical: `omit` CAN be used for matching optional fields only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- NOTE 1: **omit can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.** **omit can only be used for matching optional fields.**

requirements.original: **(…): a list of values or templates;**
requirements.canonical: The template list matching mechanism `(…)` IS a list of values or templates.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **(…): a list of values or templates;**

requirements.original: **complement (…): complement of a list of values or templates;**
requirements.canonical: The `complement (…)` matching mechanism IS the complement of a list of values or templates.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **complement (…): complement of a list of values or templates;**

requirements.original: **?: wildcard for any value;**
requirements.canonical: The AnyValue matching mechanism `?` IS a wildcard that matches any value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **?: wildcard for any value;**

requirements.original: ***: wildcard for any value or no value at all, i.e. the field is not present;**
requirements.canonical: The AnyValueOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any value or no value at all, i.e. a field that is not present.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- ***: wildcard for any value or no value at all, i.e. the field is not present;**

requirements.original: NOTE 2: *** can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be assigned to a template of any type as a whole or to an optional field of a record or set type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- NOTE 2: *** can be assigned to templates of any type as a whole or to optional fields of record and set types.

requirements.original: * can** only be used for matching optional fields.
requirements.canonical: AnyValueOrNone (`*`) CAN be used for matching optional fields only.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- * can** only be used for matching optional fields.

requirements.original: **(lowerBound** `..` _upperBound): a range of integer or float values between and including the lower- and upper_ bounds;
requirements.canonical: The range matching mechanism `(lowerBound .. upperBound)` matches integer or float values between and including the lower bound and the upper bound.

readings: The range matching mechanism applies to integer and float values only.
The range matching mechanism applies to integer and float values and, as allowed by table 11, also to character string values.
ambiguity.issue: The description mentions only integer and float values, while table 11 also allows Range for character strings; the second reading is consistent with table 11 and annex B, but the canonical keeps the stated integer/float semantics.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **(lowerBound** `..` _upperBound): a range of integer or float values between and including the lower- and upper_ bounds;

requirements.original: **superset: at least all of the elements listed, i.e. possibly more;**
requirements.canonical: The `superset` matching mechanism matches a value that contains at least all of the listed elements, and possibly more.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **superset: at least all of the elements listed, i.e. possibly more;**

requirements.original: **subset: at most the elements listed, i.e. possibly less;**
requirements.canonical: The `subset` matching mechanism matches a value that contains at most the listed elements, and possibly fewer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **subset: at most the elements listed, i.e. possibly less;**

requirements.original: **pattern: a charstring or universal charstring that matches this format;**
requirements.canonical: The `pattern` matching mechanism matches a charstring or universal charstring value that matches the given format.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **pattern: a charstring or universal charstring that matches this format;**

requirements.original: **decmatch: used for matching of encoded payload fields;**
requirements.canonical: The `decmatch` matching mechanism IS used for matching encoded payload fields.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **decmatch: used for matching of encoded payload fields;**

requirements.original: **EnumValueIdentifier with list of templates: used for matching of enumerated values with associated value** list.
requirements.canonical: An EnumValueIdentifier with a list of templates IS used for matching enumerated values with an associated value list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- **EnumValueIdentifier with list of templates: used for matching of enumerated values with associated value** list.

requirements.original: The matching mechanisms list, complemented list, subset, and superset can use the elements of a template using the all **from clause.**
requirements.canonical: The template list, complemented list, `subset` and `superset` matching mechanisms MAY use the elements of a template by means of the `all from` clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- The matching mechanisms list, complemented list, subset, and superset can use the elements of a template using the all **from clause.**

requirements.original: b) All templates and values used in the matching mechanisms above (including the referenced ones, e.g. within a pattern) shall be completely initialized.
requirements.canonical: Every template and value used in a matching mechanism used instead of values, including referenced ones such as those within a pattern, SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.2 -- b) All templates and values used in the matching mechanisms above (including the referenced ones, e.g. within a pattern) shall be completely initialized.

requirements.original: … "?"… | … "*"… | … permutation "(" { ( TemplateBody | "?" | "*" | all from TemplateInstance )[","] } ")" …
requirements.canonical: A special symbol used inside values has one of the syntaxes "?", "*" or `permutation` "(" {(TemplateBody | "?" | "*" | all from TemplateInstance) [","]} ")", each appearing inside a value notation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- … "?"… | … "*"… | … permutation "(" { ( TemplateBody | "?" | "*" | all from TemplateInstance )[","] } ")" …

requirements.original: **?: wildcard for any single element in a string, array,** `record of` or set of;
requirements.canonical: The AnyElement matching mechanism `?` IS a wildcard that matches any single element in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value.

examples.text: template bitstring mw_b := '10???'B; // where each "?" may either be 0 or 1 type record of integer RI; template RI mw_ri := {1, ?, 3} // where ? may be any integer value

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- **?: wildcard for any single element in a string, array,** `record of` or set of;

requirements.original: ***: wildcard for any number of consecutive elements in a string, array,** `record of or set of, or no` element at all (i.e. an omitted element);
requirements.canonical: The AnyElementsOrNone matching mechanism `*` IS a wildcard that matches any number of consecutive elements in a string, array, `record of` or `set of` value, or no element at all.

ambiguity.issue: "omitted element" suggests the special value omit, while what is meant is the absence of any element.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- ***: wildcard for any number of consecutive elements in a string, array,** `record of or set of, or no` element at all (i.e. an omitted element);

requirements.original: **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).
requirements.canonical: The `permutation` matching mechanism matches all of the listed elements in an arbitrary order.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).

requirements.original: **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).
requirements.canonical: AnyElement (`?`) and AnyElementsOrNone (`*`) MAY be used as elements of a permutation list.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).

requirements.original: **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).
requirements.canonical: All elements of a template MAY be added to a `permutation` by means of the `all from` clause.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- **permutation: all of the elements listed but in an arbitrary order (note, that ? and * are also allowed as** elements of the permutation list and all elements of a template can be added to permutation using the all from clause).

requirements.original: b) All templates or values used in the permutation matching mechanism shall be completely initialized.
requirements.canonical: Every template or value used in a `permutation` matching mechanism SHALL be completely initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 15.7.3 -- b) All templates or values used in the permutation matching mechanism shall be completely initialized.
